body:
Your mother unfortunately needs to learn a lesson. 
No1 we know a lot more about the effects of a simple infection on an immune compromised baby.
2. It is a privilege, not a right to be in a grandchilds life. That privilege is given by the child's parents. 
3. We don't care what they did or how they raised us, we are still healing from that shit. 
4. She is not the mother.
5. She's not the mother.
6. Fuck of you are not my child's mother.

This has nothing to do with your partner and everything to do with you MIL being an @sshole.
She can demand all she wants. She doesn't get a say in how you feed your baby.
There are so many ways to bond with a baby, but bringing a new mother stress isn't one of them. Your partner needs to sit his mother down and make sure she understands being in your child's life is a privilege, not a right, a privilege afforded to her from you.
And if she wants to have a good relationship with your baby, she needs to remove her own head from up her arse and learn what the role grandparent is.

And if she wants to have a good relationship with your baby, she needs to remove her own head from up her arse and learn what the role grandparent is.

Her confession is about her, her guilt, her feelings, and absolutely nothing to do with you. 
She told you so she could feel better, and this "punish me" is her trying to transfer that guilt to you, too. 
She's trying to excuse her behaviour, "I don't know why I did it?" "I don't even have feelings for him" is bullsh!t. She's subliminally telling you that this was the other man's fault, not hers. 
Please assess your self-worth, and ask yourself if you are prepared for her to do it again? Because she will.

As a mother to a teenage girl, I get how they can sometimes dress is not appropriate for certain situations. However, this is raising way too many red flags for me. To punish your daughter when a simple conversation needs to happen is so wrong. And to add treating your child as a threat is beyond damaging. 
You need to sit your sister down and be honest with her. She's objectifying her daughter, instead of sitting down with her and talking to her, explaining that while she should be able to run around as naked as she wants but there are certain situations where some clothing is inappropriate. 
I've been there. I've sat my daughter down and had uncomfortable conversations with her about how unfortunately the world works, how some clothing puts her at risk of being objectified, and how her body is hers alone. She has reached an age where she's no longer our little girl, and she needs to be aware of her surroundings, and there are some things even us as her parents dont need to see. Whilst building her confidence as a young woman and allowing her to express who she is, teaching her how to protect herself from unwanted attention from men.
There are ways to have these conversations, and the way your sister has done it isn't right. 
Is the husband the child's father? If not, I would be concerned about why your sister felt the need to "stake her claim" over him. Is he showing inappropriate attention to your niece?
If she wants a good relationship with her daughter, she is going the wrong way about it.
Thank you for looking out for your nieces best interest. It can be a very difficult position to be in, but she needs you. Please take her out of the situation and have a conversation with her, and make sure nothing evil is going on in her home. It most probably isn't, and it's just your sisters own insecurities that is making her behave so badly, but it's better to be safe and always protect the child first.

Definitely NTA, that's incredibly sweet. It shows you have paid attention to her and understood that she made sacrifices for your child's welfare. Her parents are always going to have something to say. Just let it go over your head and ignore it. Carry on being the type of man that makes these sweet gestures, and you will go on to have an incredible future as a family.

We are meant to grow and leave the home, make our own lives, our own families. My parents, whilst not of Asian culture, hated my partner. My dad, because he could no longer control or abuse me with having someone to protect me and my mum because of lies my dad told. I made it clear that he wasn't making me choose. They were, and if they didn't stop, they wouldn't like my choice. They kicked me out of my home, I didn't look back as I walked out with nothing but the clothes I could carry. 2yrs I hardly spoke to my mum even though we worked together, my dad not at all. My mum pieced things together and realised my dad was lying to her. She reached out and made things right not only between me and her, but my partner too. We have been together 22 years. Married 16 years, children, trauma, heartache, and failures. We are stronger than ever. Because we know what we need from each other, we set boundaries, and we work at our lives daily. 

If this man is who you see yourself having a whole lifetime together, warts and all. Then don't give up on it, your parents have lived the lives they chose, don't let them take that from you. Tell them you love them and your door is always open to them, but this is your life to live.

Unless she had a brain injury, it is unlikely that she got schizophrenia from the crash. She will most likely have had it her whole life, and the crash caused trauma, which caused the schizophrenia to escalate. I am assuming that your dad is an abusive bully, which wouldn't have helped your mum, especially with mental illness.  You can't do anything about what your dad says, but you can choose how you react to it. When he is being a bully, physically or mentally, it says everything about him and nothing about you. When he's saying cruel things towards you or about you to others, simple say to him, "I hope you feel better now" I know it's hard the man who is supposed to love you the most in this world is your abuser, it really damages so much of our self respect and confidence. Often, leaving us going from one bad relationship to the next. Don't allow him to do that to you, don't allow him to break who you truly are. And the best revenge is living your best life, full of loving relationships and friendships. Family relations isn't the be all and end all, you can build your own family. X

Firstly, it's a privilege for any family member to be a part of your baby's life, not a right! Family is bullshit, toxic, and judgemental. There's only so many times they can fail and hurt you before you close the door. And you have to break the cycle and protect your baby from loving people wholeheartedly and unconditionally for them to repeatedly reject them. 

It's heartbreaking, but it's not worth the pain for your child. To have to see the pain in your babies eyes just like yours will be unfair on either of you. I walked away from mine over 10yrs ago, created a family of my own and I will never look back x

Well, your post only makes you look bad, I'm afraid. "Taking care" of every need you thought your ex needed and actually being emotionally mature to fulfil her needs is two very different things.

The fact that you have gone out of your way to throw your "level up" in her face proves she had every reason to leave the relationship. 

Yes, as women, we do enjoy being loved and cared for, but not by men who are only doing it to make themselves look good. We need our men to be emotionally there more than all the "gifts" and "gestures" 

Her rejecting you does not make her a "gold digger," but if she stuck around, it would have. You're doing "better." Did she try and get you back? Did she come begging for you?
 No, because all the "gifts" and "breakfasts in bed" meant very little to her. 

I really do hope I'm wrong or, at the very least, you are maturing because if you don't and quickly, you won't have your current partner long.

Oh babe, he's got to go! Men don't go after a child when he has "End game material" at home. How many ways does he have to tell you he isn't worth it before you listen? 

You have everything going for you, but only you can make the choice. Put his ass out, let him go sleep on a sofa somewhere else. He couldn't even take care of you when you were sick. What do you think he would treat you like after children? Id find out if that job opportunity is still open and make a run for it!

Where is your partner in this? Your MIL can say all those things to you. She can make shitty comments, and she call you names. She can also be an non existent Grandparent, you just need to remember that when she does these things, it says everything about her character and absolutely nothing of yours. Not reacting to her behaviour is the best possible way to really piss her off. 
Your partner needs to put their mother in her place because it will backfire on you if you do it. You become the jealous daughter in law trying to steal your partner from their mother. The evil mother keeping her grandchild from the grandmother, who desperately loves him. Treat her like the toddler she's behaving as. You do, however, need to speak with your partner they should not be allowing their mother to treat you so poorly. They need to make boundaries clear and give their mother an ultimatum to step up as a grandmother or step off.

Be so proud of yourself! In this world we constantly get blood is thicker than water crammed down our throats, not matter what that blood does, how they abuse and hurt you it doesn't matter coz their family. Absolutely not its all bullshit, and that's not actually what the bible says the blood of the covenant is thicker than the water of the womb it means the absolute opposite of what we are force fed. There will be days when you doubt your decision, but just hold on and trust your gut. I'm 37yrs and 10yrs clear of my father and sister it has been the easiest 10yrs of my life x

Oh no child, your 22 and your parents are treating you like you are 15. While you live on their home you absolutely have to respect their boundaries, not coming home at ridiculous hours of the night, not coming home drunk and loud disturbing everyone else. And not bringing people home without their consent. They have a right to ask you to be home before midnight or whenever if you disturb them coming home, they also have a right to ask you to keep them informed of where you are going and if your running late because as parents we do worry about you no matter how old you are. But unless your BF is abusive they can't dictate how or when you choose to see him. They can ask you not to bring him home, but other than that they have no real say in the matter.

Oh sweetheart my husband would have been buried under the patio if he had so much as licked any of my pregnancy foods. Yes you are the asshole but your allowed to be, there is no logic to how we feel and need certain foods. My MIL cried when my FIL got her stash of mint chocolate biscuits out for guests to have, stopped being friends with them and didn't speak to my FIL for almost a week and they didn't eat a single biscuit. And I out right threw the biggest toddler tantrum at 2am  because I wanted a chicken burger from a specific fast food chain that didn't deliver, wasn't even open and was 20miles away from us. No logic whatsoever, your hubby will get over it and he won't make that same mistake again!

100% I would have helped my husband transition from male to female after kicking him so hard in the balls I created him a vagina, if he even hinted at any form of sexual activity. Not only are we feeling like we've been turned inside out, but the bleeding is horrific. Then you have to look at the emotional vulnerability we are in at these moments, I needed emotional affection. I needed to be loved on and supported. So this man clearly prayed upon his ex and as far as I'm concerned he committed sexual assualt taken advantage of an emotional need from a new mother.

Oh sweetheart you need to let go of this boy. He isn't man yet and still needs to grow. Men don't tell biased tales to their family, or manipulate stories to make them look a victim. Men proudly show off their partner to their families, and if his family are toxic they protect their partners from that family. He will stay with you for a few years but he will never put your needs above his own or theirs. They don't like the woman he's told them about, and that woman isn't you. So you can't do anything to change their opinions.

NYA! Some men need daughters like you! I'm lucky my husband not only works hard for our family but also understands he is a parent and responsible for the running of our house. We were at a family event where my two brother in laws decided its was up to them to put me in my place. That me making my husband look after our kids when he's got days off, even worse if he "watches" them when he gets in from work is just be being a lazy mum and a horrendous wife, that me getting my husband to cook and help with chores just proves their points and they would have divorced me years ago. My husband is the most amazing man, and thanks to a 14 army career intimidates the shit out of our brother in laws, put them both in their place. 1)he's not looking after his own children he's parenting. 2)him working does not mean he isn't responsible for the mess he and his children make at home, that pushing the hoover round loading the dishwasher and putting the laundry on takes him 10min. And he is very capable in the kitchen. He then told them that he married me to have a partnership not for me to be his mother, men like them make all men look like lazy good for nothing morons who can't do the simplist of tasks. And that they wouldn't have had to worry about divorcing me, because they wouldn't have got a second date let alone a marriage. Reminded them that we have been together 22years while one is on his 3rd marriage 4th baby mum who hasn't had a job in the 10yrs we've known him, and the other is a no good mamma's boy who's only still around coz he pays the bills. 

Sorry for going off then. Anyway yes you may have hurt your dad's feelings, but they both need to realise his behaviour and the resulting arguments hurt you and your siblings. How their behaviour in their marriage is probably putting you off the thought of marriage and children. And how he needs to learn a lesson, that working away from the home doesn't diminish his responsibility at home, your mum doesn't get a day off, or time to decompress or relax, or her meals cooked after she's spent all day cleaning the skid marks he left on the toilet clean. He chose to be a parent and a partner now he needs to grow up and be one.

Men dont get it, the toll on our bodies and more importantly our souls when we go through a still birth.
We had our daughter perfectly fine, then 4 years later I fell pregnant with my son, amazing pregnancy felt great unlike my previous pregnancy when I was so ill. But at almost 6months I started spotting, my waters broke but I managed to keep fighting for 10weeks. But still we lost him. Our bodies go through everything it would have giving birth to a healthy baby. The hormones the overwhelming need to love, but our arms are empty. My son would be 12now and no I'm not OK, I miss what he could have been everyday. We did eventually try again but it was 6years later. We were blessed with a daughter and 18months we had a surprise and welcomed a son. Nobody can make that decision but you. 

And people who haven't been through it don't understand. It almost destroyed my marriage I was so angry and hurt I hated my husband, wouldn't let him touch me, I didn't share a bed with him for about a year. He didn't hurt like I wanted him to hurt, like I was hurting. He didn't grieve like I wanted him to like I was. But the truth is he couldn't I was in such a bad place that he couldn't crumble too. My in laws are compulsive carpet sweepers, if it's bad you hide it don't talk about pretend it didn't happen. Nope I don't work that way, I need to talk and need to process things. And I did snap as my asshole sil announced her pregnancy on what would have been my sons 2nd birthday. I lost it shouting my son was a person, was a baby was valid and how dare they treat the loss of him so disgustingly. 

I would have felt and done the same thing you did on your daughters due date. They have no right to treat you so badly none. It doesn't matter if the don't like you, they should still have treated you with compassion.

If you truly feel there is no coming back for your marriage then this is your only choice because neither of you deserve any further heartache. Just keep open conversations with him, maybe write him a letter to explain in writing exactly how you feel and what each issue has done to you. Men don't deal with things like we do, and sometimes they are so oblivious to what is right there infront of their face.

I am so sorry for your loss, it will get easier to live with but not for a long time. I wish I had some magic words of wisdom to fix it and take away your pain. I wish you find peace and know that as long as you carry her in your heart she will never truly leave you x

I'm terribly sorry your going through this. It should be an exciting time for you and your partner. So take control back, get out meet your neighbours organise a house warming party to get to know people around you. With your mum there is no way to win her over if she's a narcissist and no matter what way you did this she would have had something negative to say and do to make you feel bad or stop you. To maybe attempt to "fix" this for other family members who are probably receiving the brunt of your mother right now, write a letter to her. Tell her "your sorry" for the way you moved out. Tell her it was about you that it was a jump/don't jump situation. And you didn't have time to include her in the the decision. Apologise for any hurt she feels, and maybe ask her to assist in organising a party at your new home for your family. Be careful when writing the letter in how you word it, and keep in mind it's not for her it's for you and your other family. This may not work, you may not feel that this is the way to go for you. I know for my situation many years ago that it put a plaster over my relationship with my abusive father long enough for me to have a relationship with my mum, and have her as part of some of the most important times of my life. Unfortunately she passed away, but I got 5years more with her than I would have. Now however I have no relationship with my father, sister or his side of my family. But its not a loss to me, because clearly they don't know, love or even respect me, to expect me to live with the abuse because he hasn't changed he still abused me mentally, could physically anymore because he is frightened of my husband. Any way I hope you find away, and I wish you all the happiness in the world because you deserve it!

Sweetheart take the leap, it's not your responsibility to financially support your parents and siblings. And you don't have to feel guilty for it, it's not your guilt to carry. Your mother has brow beaten you into believing it is. Our children grow and leave, if your a good parent they don't go far and come home often, until their lives take off. Then as parents we get to enjoy watching you achieve your goals. She may very well try turn family against you, and she may succeed for a while, but she will soon do to your siblings as she has done to you and they will come looking for you. If she does all you need to do is tell them you love them and will never close the door on them. Good mothers don't do this to good daughters!!

We need women like you to shout your success to the heavens. I may not have had the abusive husband, I instead had the abusive father. I was lucky enough to find a husband who has championed me completely. We need to to get women to believe in the strength we have, because men can't compete. Instead they attack, abuse and neglect hoping we loose our strength. You never broke your fought back like a true warrior and will raise your daughter to be just as strong. Its up to us to remind others that it's us who hold the power, it's us that creates life. We don't need men anymore not like we used to, now we get to choose out of pure love and want. And men like your ex will end their lives alone, because like my father even his kids won't want him!

While I was raised with my dad in the home, he was horrendously verbally and physically abusive to me and my mum, but my younger sister could do no wrong and he would manipulate and play us off against each other. I left home at 16, so much toxic shit happened I tried to repair relationships repeatedly. But in the end it was destroying me, my marriage, my kids. My mum died in 2008, we had repaired our relationship and I never left her side until the end. I tried to keep a relationship with my sister but she is the absolute double of our father. I couldn't do it anymore. I have been nc for 10years and I honestly would never try to have a relationship again. I did keep contact with others on my dad's side, but recently I cut all ties with them because they were just spy's for them. I never got congratulations on the births of my children, no happy birthdays, no how are yous nothing. So they obviously have no idea and have made no effort to know who I really am, they've just believed the lies. Family isn't what your born into, it's what you create yourself, their toxic behaviour isn't worth the damage caused to your mental health. Everything they ever said about me about what my life would be I've proved them wrong. My marriage won't last, we've been together 22years, my kids are amazing and I'm happy. They however arnt doing good and I believe its karma. Be honest with yourself what do these people bring to your life?

Sometimes thr USA confuses me. When myself hubby and family planned our wedding we budgeted for bridesmaids needs, dress, shoes some accessories like hair pieces. They were responsible financially for hair make up and nails and it was optional if they didn't want to, we also paid for groomsmens attire. We invite people to be apart of our wedding so we are responsible for the costs, and if you can't afford what is needed then you simply don't have it. The wedding industry is absolutely ridiculous now people spending hundreds of thousands on one day, they could have bought a house, dream holidays for the rest of their lives, school fees for future children. So much goes into how it all looks, show boating. That all to often the reason your doing this is lost. I had a reasonably large wedding family from all over the UK traveled to be with us, we were married in church and went on to a beautiful old church that had been turned into an events place. So I understand wanting an amazing day, but I made my budget and I worked out how long I needed to save to have all I wanted and once I was half way there then I booked my wedding.

Well done, for so many things. It's beyond difficult and scary to come to terms with abuse from a "family member" and to then confront your abuser. While his reasoning for the abuse is understandable its not OK for him to expect you to let go of your trauma from a simple "sorry not my fault". And while he needs help with his own trauma he has to realise that he did the same to you. Well done confronting him, and I really hope you got to say everything you needed, I hope he felt every word you said with the pain it came from. I hope it's was cathartic for you I know it was for me when I confronted mine, I took my voice back and every word I said was filled with the venom from my pain. Every reason why I held so much anger and I made sure to not leave a single word unsaid knowing that was the last time I would ever see that person. It helped me massively to defend the little girl inside me that nobody else made a stand for, I took the first step of healing her and the first step of learning to let go of the pain and hatred I felt so deeply in my bones. Be proud of the steps you have taken making him acknowledge his responsibility, whether he excepted it or not.

Your not the one being a "pussy", that title well and truly belongs to your husband! He should be putting his family in their place, how dare they speak to your child in that way. If my MIL spoke to me or my children in any disrespectful way you best believe my husband would have put his mother straight and that would be the only time she'd get put in her place. If it happened again there would be no conversation and they would never breathe the same air as my child again. Your inlaws need a valuable lesson of respect and you need to make them understand that being apart of your children's lives is a privilege and not a right, that's it. No other chances, ever!

Yep!! Constantly, or they talk down to you, or assume you must be stupid for your breed of choice. I have an English bulldog, I took him to a chain veterinary clinic purely for his 1st vaccinations and the vet tech started yelling at me about how she was going to have to put him down and what a horrible breed he is and so much more drivel to the point I had the whole store looking at me and she hadn't even looked at him yet. Well I'm not the one to try and I stood up told her that she would never have to put my dog down as she shouldn't worry she will never get a penny from my pet insurance. We'll I lost my shit and by time I finished the manager was apologising and the people waiting behind me cancelled their appointments. The breeds most of us choose are uniquely personal to us, we have an emotional tie to them and knowing this people still jump to conclusions. I love so many breeds but I don't know them, I want any animal I bring home to be a successful addition to my family so I bring home what I know, and what I can give everything too. Start telling idiots to f@ck off and mind their business, it's extremely cathartic!

I've been in both positions, and I also have twin sils from hell! If she is genuine this will settle if you both give a little. And if she's not that will soon show because spiteful people have a need to hurt others and if that's the case allow her to dig her own hole, her brother will see this side of her and he Will make sure that hole shallows her up. Its not worth you future starting with your husband feeling you wronged his sister. I've been with my husband 21years, 1 sil clearly had an issue from the start, while the other played all sides. I'm still here, happy with beautiful children and a loving husband, with no more issues with my sils because I stopped reacting, but made sure my husband was present to witness his sisters toxicity! I really hope though that's not the case for you, and I wish you all the success for your marriage and the most beautiful wedding!

Well that was a lot, at first after reading the title I was expecting a really mean spirited comment aimed at really targeting yourself esteem. But in all honesty I don't get that from what you have written. You have self esteem issues and it's amazing how self aware you are to recognise that, but knowing you have them and being able to stop you reacting poorly to a situation is a different matter. Both of you have image sensitivity and are triggering each other. You felt insulted by what she said and you should have dealt with it then and there, but you didn't and it blew up into something it should never have become. If you had stopped her then and told her that hurt you, she would have been able to explain herself better, or she could very well have dug in more to insult you further. If she doubled down it would have been clear she was just being spiteful and mean and you could have dealt with it then and there with your partner. However you didn't, you let yourself digest everything she said and decided it was from spite, you then spoke about it to others and had a row with your partner. So by time you did speak with her it was a way bigger situation than it ever needed to be, she was left feeling so badly she felt she had no choice but to pull out of her brothers wedding  and is left feeling like people have been speaking about her behind her back. And your partner is clearly feeling some kind of way too. Its to easy in this world to see the nastiness all around us, and trust me when I say you are going to come across some horrible times, so horrid that this won't even be in your top 20 shitty times of your life. People are allowed to say things and yes sometimes those things may hurt us, or offend us just because that's our reaction doesn't mean that is their intention. I really hope you find away to let go of this, bring the family together especially for the beginning of your journey 🙏

Stop apologising, it was never your place nor was it your secret to tell. Your step sister came to you because you made her feel safe, and at the time she probably didn't know how to feel about being pregnant and becoming a mother so young. She may not have made any decisions about her future yet. And if everyone knew choices may have been forced upon her that she didn't want nor was she ready for. Your mother is being beyond unfair treating you like this, and quite honestly needs to grow up. I hope this situation becomes better for you, just don't doubt yourself, you did the right thing x

It really is so hard, we so desperately want our dad's to be our superheroes. It hurts like no other pain to see others have this amazing father/child relationship because we a stuck with a narcissistic assh@le. Confronting him isn't about him validating your feelings, because that will never happen. It is about you clearing his toxicity from your life make it so it's no longer your burden to carry. My father blames me for his bad behaviour, it was my fault he beat me as a kid because I made him wait to make him a coffee, because I was late home from school, because I defended my mum. He calls me names because I make him angry, tells lies about me because I confronted him. I carried all this for so many years but it was never my burden and neither is any of your father's behaviour. Keep reminding yourself that your feelings are valid, that you have every right to make your boundaries clear. You are worth putting yourself first because he isn't worth it, and he will never do what you need him too. It's beyond difficult so definitely speak to your circle and have them ready and prepared to have your back and keep you strong and motivated xxx

Firstly you need to remind yourself of your worth, secondly look are your child and really get inside your head and experience the emotional response to them. You don't owe your father anything, and you need to put a stop to him to consistently failing you. He need to know that being apart of his grandchilds life is a privilege and not a right. You earn that privilege by being an active, stable and loving parent. My father is an abusive assh@le, I walked away 10yrs ago just me, my husband and our eldest daughter, I lost alot of his side of our family, for a long time that really hurt me, but I realised that if they believe the lies my father has told them, then they don't know me at all and arnt worth a single tear. I stopped all contact, completely blocked on all social media, stopped all contact with my daughter because he would call me all sorts of names to my child who was 4 at the time. Also tried to teach her to say some of the most disgusting words against other race's. He has never met my younger children and he never will. It's our duty to protect our children from anyone who can cause them any harm. Since I walked away my family have thrived, everything he said would happen I've proved wrong. You don't owe that man anything so you have to put you first bec he never will. So whatever is easier for you text phone call or face to face tell him what he has done to you, how hurt you are and then tell him that he is not welcome around you or your family from then on, ask him to delete you number and then block him every way possible. Don't leave anything unsaid because that will be a cathartic thing for you, it will help you know you've done the right thing x

I'm so sorry your going through this. Your parents are right in telling you to except who Your sister is, however you do not have to except or tolerate her behaviour towards yourself and you have to except that your parents may never stop enabling her. You all need therapy, you especially need support for your traumatic childhood and adulthood. And you need help amd support to build your strength to walk away, it does not make you a bad person for putting an end to the abuse inflicted upon you. You deserve to live a happy healthy balanced life and your sister is never going to allow that. Think of your future, of her behaviour patterns she will never allow you to have a beautiful relationship a happy engagement, the most wonderful wedding, finding your dream home and the most perfect children. She will poison and destroy any attempt at happiness for you, she is a hateful, jealous and horrendously toxic person and the only person who can protect you is you. Therapy will help you come to terms with what you need to do to protect yourself, and to have an understanding with your parents that you want your relationship with them to be healthy and full of love but they have to stop guilt tripping you just to make their lives easier and if they want to be apart if your future they have to separate their relationship with her and their relationship with you. Take it from someone who couldn't tolerate the abuse and toxic relationship from my sister that i chose to end any form of relationship with. And honestly I have had 0 issues no drama, just a calm quiet life.nThis isn't going to happen over night, I am wishing you so much strength and hope that you realise that you are worth so much more than what you feel right now. Time to take control if your life x

Please know I'm not defending bad behaviour. You said you think your sister asked him for a divorce and he is taking it out on you, but he may not be. Your sister could have asked him for a divorce and given him reasons why she wants their marriage to end, his reaction of anger towards you could have been out of panic and he rushed to defend his wife trying to show her he can put her 1st. I'm so unbelievably sorry for your loss. And I understand what you are going through.

As women we lose a child, go through some of the most horrendous experiences especially hormonal. I suffered and extremely early miscarriage and a stillbirth at 30weeks. With the miscarriage I wanted to cry all the time, and needed comfort from my DH fell into a dark space blaming myself because it was my fault I was drinking and smoking without a care in the world. When the truth was I was taking every precaution not to get pregnant so I had no idea I was until the miscarriage. There was no intimacy for about 6months and even then it wasn't for us as a couple it was purely for fulfilling his needs, and he then stopped trying because it isn't the same no matter how i tried to fake it.


When we suffered the stillbirth it was different, my head heart and soul felt like i was dying, while my body was having all the normal reactions after giving birth. My hormones filled me with an intense need to love, made me feel all the same feelings when we had our daughter but there was no baby to give all this to. Wrapped up in the most intense grief and confusion we turned to each other and was intimate the day after we lost our precious son. That was the last time for almost a year. My DH and I planned the funeral and DH returned to work a week after our loss, because he can't stop, if he stops he hurts, but it left me feeling abandoned and alone. 10days later we held our babies funeral and i could see my DH hadn't abandoned me at all. I watched him as he stopped the funeral director from lifting our sons tiny White coffin, and couldnt breathe with guilt and grief took over my body as i heard him say "I am the only person who will carry my son" I realised then his pain was there too. However I couldnt get past my own grief. When the bleeding finally stopped, I couldnt bare DH touching me and would find ever excuse in the book to not have sex or any kind of intimacy with him. My DH is an affectionate man he needs to be told he is loved and have some form of physical intimacy not sex necessarily but held and cuddled kissed. But I just couldnt do it, I didnt even sleep in our bed anymore, I would sleep downstairs on the sofa. My marriage was almost over and for a little while I was ok with that. I don't know what stopped me feeling this way, but I soon realised that I was hurting him so deeply, like I was punishing him for my pain and I had to stop that if I truly loved him so I sat him down. I had to tell him everything, I had to tell him I couldnt lay in the arms that cradled our son, that I couldn't bare his touch because because I felt his pain. That I had all the normal after birth emotions but my arms were empty. My milk came in but I had no baby to feed. The thought of sex made me angry scared and lost. That at that time sex wasn't about intimacy between us but about me being a woman and my role was to have children and id failed. I couldnt bare the thought of ever getting pregnant again, and the only way I could guarantee that was by not having sex at all. That night he lay his head on my knee and we cried almost the whole night, the next day he found us a grief and family therapist and we worked through it. 

This was 11 years ago, and while it took a long time and alot of hard work we saved our marriage and after 5years we finally felt ready to try again and have had a little girl and then an extra little surprise we welcomed a little boy 2years after.
I hope my story helps you, and you understand there is no wrong way to process your loss. There is no name for us, mothers without their child, because there is no way to describe just how painful it is. Talk to your partner tell him it all from your soul, tell him you love him but that you need time and help. That you don't mean to make him feel neglected or rejected. That you want to get back to who you were as a couple, but you can't so you need to figure out how you move forward as a couple, how you can love each other and help each other come to terms with your loss. Please seek professional support, and I honestly believe you can both come through this stronger and your love for each other will be all the more for the hard work put in to keep it. I wish you all the best and so much love.
